description:
Found while building fz-3ul.1: src/ir_interp charges no reductions anywhere, so no interpreted loop ever yields and process_exited.reduction_yields is always 0 on interp. Fixture 00720 (100_000 raising iterations) yields 150 times on JIT and AOT and 0 times on interp; a plain tail loop with no try shows the same. The reduction-yielding doc claims interpreter parity. The runtime test for 00720 on the interpreter therefore asserts delivery and completion only.

Acceptance: the interpreter charges reductions at the same points the compiled code does (one authority for where a reduction is spent, shared or mirrored and tested as equal); reduction_yields on interp for 00720 is >= 1 and the interp runtime test asserts it like the JIT one; three-path parity on the fixture matrix; the doc that claims parity is made true or corrected to the facts; gate green.

Since fz-gl6.3 (652c3016c) the interpreter ends every quantum through sched_core::end_quantum and roots its parked receive's refs via BackendSchedulerAdapter::collect_heap. That code relies on the interpreter never yielding: collect_heap asserts no backend_resume entry exists at a quantum's end, and drive_backend_until_idle returns an error on Disposition::Requeue. Making the interpreter yield must root the backend_resume entry (args, env, continuations) in collect_heap the same way and replace the Requeue error with a requeue; both asserts will fire loudly until then.
title: The interpreter charges reductions so an interpreted loop yields like a compiled one
